title: Reliability is a user-specific property of large language models
abstract: arXiv:2611.23732v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Public benchmarks support comparisons of large language model (LLM) capabilities, yet users can experience the same highly ranked model differently. Drawing on traditional software reliability, we argue that the reliability of an LLM service should be assessed for specified users and conditions of use. This requires more than a capability score: evaluation evidence must support a claim about failure during future operation. We distinguish testing to discover faults from testing to assess reliability and identify ten modelling considerations behind such claims. We propose a six-workstream research roadmap linking claim specification, dynamic operational profiles, graded outcomes and noisy judgements, local probabilistic robustness, interaction dependence, and statistical inference with reassessment. Local probabilistic robustness addresses the behavioural variation hidden when different concrete inputs are treated as the same task. Publ

translated_title: 可靠性是大型语言模型的用户特定属性
translated_abstract: 公开基准测试支持对大型语言模型（LLM）能力的比较，但用户对同一高排名模型的实际体验可能各不相同。借鉴传统软件可靠性理论，我们认为LLM服务的可靠性应针对特定用户和特定使用条件进行评估。这不仅仅是能力分数的问题：评估证据必须能够支持关于未来运行中故障的论断。我们区分了用于发现缺陷的测试与用于评估可靠性的测试，并识别了支撑此类论断的十个建模考量因素。我们提出了一个包含六个研究方向的研究路线图，涵盖论断规范、动态操作剖面、分级结果与噪声判断、局部概率鲁棒性、交互依赖性以及带重评估的统计推断。局部概率鲁棒性解决了将不同具体输入视为同一任务时所隐藏的行为变异问题。
tldr: 该论文提出LLM服务的可靠性应针对特定用户和使用条件进行评估，并据此提出了包含论断规范、动态操作剖面、局部概率鲁棒性等六个方向的研究路线图。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that LLM service reliability should be assessed for specified users and conditions of use, proposing a six-workstream research roadmap covering claim specification, dynamic operational profiles, and local probabilistic robustness.
